abstract: A statistical analysis was made by computer on 511 cases of testicular tumor experienced at 14 facilities in Japan between 1970 and 1979. The age distribution of the patients had two peaks, one under 3 years (15%) and the other between 25 and 34 years (32%). Forty percent of the patients were office workers and 76% were college graduates. Fifty percent of the patients had 0 to 1 sibs. The blood type distribution was similar to that for the whole Japanese population. Six percent of the patients had a past history of trauma, and no relation with cell type was detected. Sixty nine percent of the patients were married and 31% were not married. Sixty seven percent of the patients over 30 had seminoma, and 78% of the patients under 29 years old had non-seminoma. Seminoma was rare in patients under 9 years old. Histologically, 75% were simple type, and 25% were mixed type. Forty three percent of the cases were seminoma and 57% were non-seminoma. Of the stage I cases, 78% and 57%, and of the stage III cases 7 and 28%, respectively, were seminoma and non-seminoma, many of the non-seminoma being at high stage. The 5-year survival rate for the 75 patients under 9 years old was 96%, and that for the 341 patients over 15 years was 70%, the survival rate for the patients under 9 years being significantly higher. The 5-year survival rate for stage I, II and III seminoma was 100, 65 and 0%, respectively, while that for non-seminoma was 93, 56 and 8%, respectively. The survival rate for stage I was higher for seminoma cases than for non-seminoma cases. No difference was detected between survival rate for stage II or III between seminoma and non-seminoma. The survival rate for seminoma did not differ with the time when the surgery was performed, but for the patients with non-seminomatous tumors, the survival rate was higher for the patients operated within one month than those operated later. The survival rate was not related to the weight of the extracted testicle. The 5-year survival rate for the patients with normal body temperature was 78% whereas that for the patients who had fevers was 32%. The 5-year survival rate for the patients not accompanied by abdominal tumors was about 80%, whereas that for the patients with palpated abdominal tumors was 42%.(ABSTRACT TRUNCATED AT 400 WORDS)
abstract_ja: 1970年から1979年の間に日本の14施設で経験した精巣腫瘍511例についてコンピュータによる統計解析を行った。患者の年齢分布は2つのピークを示し、一つは3歳未満（15%）、もう一つは25～34歳（32%）であった。患者の40%は会社員、76%は大学卒業者であった。50%の患者は兄弟姉妹が0～1人であった。血液型分布は日本人全体とほぼ同様であった。6%の患者に外傷の既往があったが、組織型との関連は認められなかった。69%の患者が既婚、31%が未婚であった。30歳以上の患者の67%がセミノーマ、29歳以下の患者の78%が非セミノーマであった。9歳未満ではセミノーマはまれであった。組織学的には75%が単純型、25%が混合型であった。症例の43%がセミノーマ、57%が非セミノーマであった。病期I症例のうちセミノーマは78%、非セミノーマは57%、病期III症例ではそれぞれ7%と28%がセミノーマおよび非セミノーマであり、非セミノーマの多くは進行病期であった。9歳未満の75例の5年生存率は96%、15歳以上の341例では70%で、9歳未満の患者の生存率は有意に高かった。病期I、II、IIIのセミノーマの5年生存率はそれぞれ100%、65%、0%であり、非セミノーマでは93%、56%、8%であった。病期Iの生存率はセミノーマ症例の方が非セミノーマ症例より高かった。病期IIまたはIIIの生存率はセミノーマと非セミノーマで差がなかった。セミノーマの生存率は手術時期によって差がなかったが、非セミノーマ性腫瘍の患者では、1か月以内に手術を受けた患者の生存率が後に手術を受けた患者より高かった。生存率は摘出した精巣の重量とは関連がなかった。平熱の患者の5年生存率は78%であったのに対し、発熱のあった患者では32%であった。腹部腫瘤を触知しなかった患者の5年生存率は約80%であったのに対し、腹部腫瘤を触知した患者では42%であった。（抄録は400語で打ち切られている）
